Your Grace,

Here’s a concise, production-ready plan to finish the Obsidian plugin, aligned with your workspace rules (Result pattern, accessibility, TypeScript strictness, and no-any), and minimizing risk.

### What’s already solid
- Core plugin flow is implemented: settings, commands, views, context menus, markdown postprocessor.
- Tagging pipeline via `initializeCore` with proper Result/error handling and retries.
- Auto-sync hooks in `DocumentTagService` and CM6 tag widget.
- Tests and build setup present.

### Gaps to finish
- Key storage “system” option is not implemented (currently always local).
- Status/notice streams aren’t wired to UI handlers.
- Accessibility/UX polish (labels, keyboard ops, contrast).
- Minor link/content fixes and consistent behavior for “statusBarDisplay”.

### Proposed completion plan
1) Key storage implementation (safe, no extra native deps)
- Implement a storage strategy interface in `KeyManager`:
  - LocalStorageStorage: keep as-is (base64 obfuscation).
  - SystemLikeSecureStorage: use WebCrypto AES‑GCM with a derived key (manifest id + random salt stored once). This is stable in Electron/Obsidian, doesn’t require native keychain libraries, and is a meaningful security upgrade over base64.
- Behavior:
  - If user chooses “system”, store via AES‑GCM; if crypto API is unavailable (edge), fall back to local with a clear Notice.
- Stability: WebCrypto in Electron is mature and stable. Avoids immature/fragile keychain packages in Obsidian plugin contexts.

2) Wire UI handlers to service streams (predictable UX)
- Instantiate `StatusBarHandler` when `statusBarDisplay !== 'never'` to subscribe to `TaggingService.status`.
- Instantiate `NoticeHandler` with `(msg) => new Notice(msg)` to subscribe to `TaggingService.notice`.
- Honor `statusBarDisplay`:
  - always: always visible.
  - processing: show on processing, hide when idle.
  - never: remove/unsubscribe.
- Stability: Trivial, aligns with your observable-based UI layer pattern.

3) Accessibility & UX improvements (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- `TagManagementView`:
  - Add labels/aria to search and buttons; ensure keyboard focus order and roles.
  - Ensure counts/text meet contrast; minimum 16px text; consistent heading hierarchy.
- `TagVisualizationView`:
  - Add labels for zoom/filter, keyboard alternatives for zoom and navigation.
  - Prefer calmer color palette and ensure contrast for node text; avoid motion triggers (pause animation with a toggle).
- Styles (`styles.css`):
  - Accessible focus states for `.magus-mark-tag-widget`, clear hover/active states; ensure 44x44px touch target minimum where interactive.

4) Settings polish and content fixes
- Update “Documentation” and GitHub links in `MagusMarkSettingTab` to `https://github.com/neurotypic-ai/magus-mark`.
- Clarify “System” storage help text (uses OS-backed crypto when available; otherwise secure local encryption fallback).

5) Minor behavior refinements
- Respect “processing” mode by hiding status when idle (driven by `status$`).
- Keep CM6 tag widget but ensure it doesn’t disrupt editing (it currently uses Decoration.replace; we’ll keep interaction simple and accessible; add a title attribute).
- Throttle auto-sync already delayed 5s—good. Add guard against re-entrancy with a simple per-path cooldown map.

6) Build, test, package
- Run plugin tests; fix any lint/types (no disables).
- Build and package via `pnpm run package`.
- Sanity test in Obsidian desktop.

### Risks and tradeoffs
- “System” storage via WebCrypto is secure and stable but not a literal OS keychain. It avoids brittle native deps and works in Obsidian; we’ll document this clearly in settings.
- CM6 tag widget replacement could impact screen readers; we’ll add `aria-label`/`role="button"` and ensure keyboard activation.

### Your decisions before I proceed
- Key storage: Approve WebCrypto AES‑GCM “system” storage in-plugin (secure, no native deps) with fallback and clear messaging?
- Tag widget: Keep Decoration.replace chip (with a11y), or prefer underline/mark decoration to avoid replacement semantics?
- Status bar “processing”: OK to auto-hide when idle?

Reply “YOLOFUCKIT” and I’ll implement immediately; otherwise, confirm the options and I’ll proceed accordingly.

Your Humble Servant, Sebastién
